biological.citation: Cognitive and Synaptic Impairment Induced by Deficiency of Autism Risk Gene Smarcc2 and its Rescue by Histone Deacetylase Inhibition (PMID: 40492195)
biological.summary: SMARCC2 was significantly diminished in iPSC-derived neurons from idiopathic ASD patients. Smarcc2 deficiency in mouse prefrontal cortex led to impaired working memory, downregulation of synaptic transmission genes, and impaired GABAergic and glutamatergic synaptic currents. Treatment with the HDAC inhibitor romidepsin restored histone acetylation, working memory, and synaptic gene expression in Smarcc2-deficient mice.

biological.citation: SMARCC2 silencing suppresses oncogenic activation through modulation of chromatin accessibility in breast cancer (PMID: 38852505)
biological.summary: SMARCC2 silencing in breast cancer cells suppressed tumorigenesis and reduced cancer stem cell features, revealing a pro-tumorigenic function for SMARCC2 in breast cancer that contrasts with other SWI/SNF subunits. Mechanistically, SMARCC2 depletion downregulated the Ras-PI3K signaling pathway by reducing chromatin accessibility at enhancers of key genes such as PIK3CB. These findings were validated using RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP analyses, and xenograft models.

biological.citation: Elucidating the clinical and molecular spectrum of SMARCC2-associated NDD in a cohort of 65 affected individuals (PMID: 37551667)
biological.summary: Missense variants in SMARCC2 were examined using 3D protein modeling, co-immunoprecipitation, and proximity-ligation assays, revealing decreased protein expression for N-terminal missense variants similar to likely gene-disrupting variants. Non-truncating variants clustered in functional domains and were mostly de novo, associated with severe developmental delay, while LGD variants were predominantly inherited and associated with milder phenotypes. These findings suggest distinct pathomechanisms for different variant classes affecting BAF complex subunit interactions.

biological.citation: Nuclear RIPK1 promotes chromatin remodeling to mediate inflammatory response (PMID: 35661830)
biological.summary: Activated nuclear RIPK1 mediates phosphorylation of SMARCC2, a key component of the BAF complex, to promote chromatin remodeling and transcription of specific proinflammatory genes. The RIPK1/BAF complex is recruited by specific transcription factors to active enhancers and promoters marked by H3K4me1 and H3K27ac upon RIPK1 activation. Increased nuclear RIPK1 activation and RIPK1/BAF-mediated chromatin-remodeling activity were found in cells expressing non-cleavable RIPK1 and in ALS pathological samples.

biological.citation: FBXO28 promotes proliferation, invasion, and metastasis of pancreatic cancer cells through regulation of SMARCC2 ubiquitination (PMID: 37348029)
biological.summary: FBXO28 was identified as an E3 ligase that targets SMARCC2 for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation in pancreatic cancer. Upregulation of SMARCC2 reversed the pro-tumorigenic effects of FBXO28 overexpression on proliferation, invasion, and metastasis of pancreatic cancer cells. FBXO28 expression was negatively correlated with SMARCC2 levels and with patient survival prognosis.

biological.citation: SMARCC2 mediates the regulation of DKK1 by the transcription factor EGR1 through chromatin remodeling to reduce the proliferative capacity of glioblastoma (PMID: 36418306)
biological.summary: SMARCC2 acts as a tumor suppressor in glioblastoma by negatively regulating transcription of the oncogene DKK1 through chromatin remodeling, closing the DKK1 promoter region bound by transcription factor EGR1. SMARCC2 knockout promoted glioblastoma cell proliferation while overexpression inhibited it, and in vivo overexpression significantly reduced intracranial glioma size in nude mice. The SWIRM domain of SMARCC2 was found to play a more important role than the SANT domain in its chromatin remodeling function.

biological.citation: Expanding the Spectrum of BAF-Related Disorders: De Novo Variants in SMARCC2 Cause a Syndrome with Intellectual Disability and Developmental Delay (PMID: 30580808)
biological.summary: Transcriptomic analysis of fibroblasts from individuals with SMARCC2 variants identified differentially expressed genes with roles in neuronal development and function, including H19, SCRG1, RELN, and CACNB4. SMARCC2 (BAF170) is described as an invariable core subunit of the BAF complex crucial for embryogenesis and corticogenesis. Fifteen individuals with heterozygous SMARCC2 variants presented with neurodevelopmental delay, with more severe phenotypes in those harboring variants in the SANT and SWIRM DNA-interacting domains.

biological.citation: The functional landscape of the human phosphoproteome (PMID: 31819260)
biological.summary: Machine learning analysis of 119,809 human phosphosites identified regulatory phosphosites in SMARCC2 that were experimentally validated to play a role in neuronal differentiation. SMARCC2 is identified as a member of the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling complex with functionally important phosphorylation sites. This study integrated 59 features of proteomic, structural, regulatory, and evolutionary relevance to prioritize functional phosphosites.

biological.citation: Identification of selective SWI/SNF dependencies in enzalutamide-resistant prostate cancer (PMID: 39905188)
biological.summary: A systematic CRISPR epigenetic library screen identified SMARCC2 as selectively essential in enzalutamide-resistant prostate cancer models. Chromatin occupancy of SMARCC2 and BRG1 was expanded in enzalutamide resistance at regions overlapping with CRPC-associated transcription factors accessible in clinical samples. These findings reveal a regulatory role for SMARCC2 in enzalutamide-resistant prostate cancer and support targeting the SWI/SNF complex in late-stage disease.

biological.citation: ASHG 2014 - The discovery of integrated gene networks for autism (O. Penn et al.)
biological.summary: SMARCC2 was identified as part of a significant gene module (p<0.005) enriched for de novo mutations in ASD and ID patients, associated with the SWI/SNF and NCOR complexes and showing highest expression early during embryonic development. SMARCC2 was also found in an overlapping module for schizophrenia, with mutations observed in both ASD/ID and schizophrenia cohorts. The module containing SMARCC2 was associated with Wnt and Notch signaling pathways.
biological.sample_size: 1116 ASD/ID patients; 2661 in full SSC analysis
